facts.quote: The Agni Purana does not include the Matrikas among the yoginis, but states that they are related. It divides the yoginis into 8 family groups, each one led by a Matrika, who is either the mother or another relative of each of her yoginis.
facts.text: Chapter 52 of the Agni Purana details 64 yoginis divided into eight primary family groups led by distinct Matrika mother deities.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The Agni Purana, the Skanda Purana and the Kalika Purana each contain two lists (namavalis) of yoginis with often wholly differing contents.
facts.text: The Kalika Purana and Skanda Purana enumerate distinct namavalis listing sixty-four yoginis invoked as emanations of feminine divine energy.

facts.label: scripture

facts.text: The Sri Matottara Tantra describes the spatial geometry of the Yogini Chakra as a circular configuration designed for esoteric rituals.

sheet.summary: Local legends portray the hilltop shrine at Mitaoli as an ancient centre for tantric astrology and a gathering place of the sixty-four battle yoginis of lore. Archaeological investigations revealed a circular hypaethral temple containing sixty-four outer chambers and an epigraph dating to 1323 CE during the reign of Devapala. A major point of dispute surrounds claims that the old Parliament House was copied from Mitaoli, as historians emphasize the total lack of archival documentation linking the British architects to the site despite the striking visual resemblance. It remains unknown which specific yogini sculptures originally occupied the perimeter cells before they were lost and replaced by Shiva lingas.
